The '''17th Academy Awards''' were held on March 15, 1945, at [[Grauman's Chinese Theatre]], honoring the films of [[1944 in film|1944]]. This was the first time the complete awards ceremony was broadcast nationally, on the [[Blue Network]] (later [[Cumulus Media Networks|ABC Radio]]). [[Bob Hope]] hosted the 70-minute broadcast, which included film clips that required explanation for the radio audience.<ref name="Dunning">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EwtRbXNca0oC&dq=%22The+Academy+Awards+Show%22&pg=PA4 |last=Dunning| first=John| author-link=John Dunning (detective fiction author) | title=On the Air: The Encyclopedia of Old-Time Radio| date=1998| publisher=Oxford University Press| location=New York, NY| isbn=978-0-19-507678-3| pages=4–5 | edition=Revised| access-date=2019-10-01}}</ref>

[[Darryl F. Zanuck]] and [[20th Century-Fox]] spent a fortune promoting ''[[Wilson (1944 film)|Wilson]]'' out of determination to have it win the Best Picture Oscar, but it lost to ''Going My Way'', which made Zanuck bitter.<ref name="Oscars '44 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/836/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=836 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref>

This year was notable for being the only time an individual was nominated for two acting awards for the ''same role'' in the ''same film'': [[Barry Fitzgerald]] received nominations for both [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] and [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] for his performance as Father Fitzgibbon in the Best Picture winner ''[[Going My Way]]''. Fitzgerald won for Best Supporting Actor, while his co-star [[Bing Crosby]] won Best Actor.
